newsitem.title: CHINA: China widens foreign exchange trading limits.
newsitem.headline: China widens foreign exchange trading limits.

text.p: The People's Bank of China has relaxed the limits on foreign exchange trading on the China Foreign Exchange Trade system, the national interbank market based in Shanghai, a central bank statement said on Thursday.

As from Wednesday, the limit for one transaction against the previous transaction of the Chinese yuan versus the U.S. dollar and the Hong Kong dollar has been widened to 100 points against 20 points, the statement said.

The statement said the limit of 1,000 points for a Japanese yen transaction against the previous transaction, with the trading unit being 100 yen against the Chinese yuan, remains in place, the statement said.
The limits, which have been in force since the foreign exchange market was set up in April 1994, are aimed at stabilising the market and the yuan rate.
There are also daily rate movement limits of 0.3 percent in either direction for the U.S. dollar against the yuan, one percent for the Hong Kong dollar and 0.3 percent for 100 Japanese yen.
"The daily movement limits for each of the currencies in one session will remain unchanged," the central bank statement said.
Traders said the relaxation of the limit on the rate change from one transaction to the next was likely to result in more lively foreign exchange trading on the market.
But with daily limits still in force and the central bank often intervening in trading, the rates are unlikely to fluctuate sharply, they said.

"Trading is expected to be more active," said one trader. "But the Chinese yuan is likely to continue to be one of the most stable currencies in the world due to the daily limits and frequent central bank intervention."
